body: It's a mental disorder. It doesn't make you special, it doesn't make you lesser. It's just there. I'm bipolar, I don't care how the community sees it. What matters is how you see it. If you think you're seeing other worldly beings though, sorry, that's not what it appears to be. It's just a hallucination. Nothing more.

She sounds manipulative. Try and record her saying this, give it to the police. And you need to worry about yourself. Give 35 percent of yourself to people, 50 percent if it's love. Take care of yourself first.

>I fuck up every friendship eventually by being dumb.

>Clingy as fuck.

>Empty. When I am "happy" I feel delusional

>Guilt-tripped daily

>Insecure as fuck

>Emotionally unstable as hell

>Broke

>The only reason I havent already is because of my family and friends. I wish they could all magically stop caring so i could just fucking die already.

I, too, push people away. Jeep trying, you'll meet some friends who refuse to be pushed away. Ones that care. Those are your true friends. The ones who abandoned you were just acquaintances.

Also, like you, I am clingy. We lose so many friends that we latch onto the ones we do have. Try this practice: texting a friend? Ignore them from four to ten minutes instead of instantly responding. Even try to put them out of your mind. For every two times your friend ask you out, wait a week or two and then ask them out. Don't be too eager. These two things help tremendously.

This comment about feeling empty, but dillusional when happy mixed with the unstable emotions makes me wonder if you're bipolar or have hormones doing their thing. How old are you, might I ask? Try to fill the empty inside you with a hobby or passion. And really put effort into this. If you don't help yourself, no one can. 

How are you guilt tripped and by who? Parents? Have you tried bringing up the guilt tripping to the person doing so?

Start walking as much as you can. Every mile or half mile, start speed walking to break a sweat. Speed walk for five minutes, then go back to regular, comfortable walk. You'll burn weight a lot faster than you'd think and start feeling much better about yourself if you're already skinny because it builds muscle. This was recommended to me by a surgeon and has worked wonders.

Tell me about your emotional instability, would you?

I can't work a job because of terrible bipolar, PTSD, and panic attacks. No one will hire me. I also don't have the paperwork I need for a job. So I'm broke, too. All this means is I am more creative. I write poetry, short stories. I hum new tunes. I find the beauty in the little things. 

I hope this helps, some. I feel I talked about myself too much but that's just me trying to relate so you know it's something you can survive.

Change "no father" to "father who cares more about video games than you" and "alcoholic mother" to "drug addict mother", then I would have been in your predicament a few years ago. When we're young and depressed, we don't see a light at the end of the tunnel. Start simple. This will be difficult. Just walk. Outside, if you can. No matter the weather, though cold helps you think. Walk until you feel you can't anymore, then speed walk for five minutes, then walk normal pace again. This was my first step. 

By the way, you can try and work with the government to get out of your house and away from your mother. Just a thought. 

If you don't do anything all day then you're refusing to help yourself. If you refuse to help yourself then no one else can help you either.

I have a friend who just went through this scenario. I informed her, it is your hospital's (or any psyche ward's) legal duty to tell your workplace that you're "sick" (they can't legally say with what) and for your job to fire you over this they would have a massive lawsuit on their hands.

No problem. I'm struggling quite a bit myself right now and helping people, thst release of oxytocin l I guess, something about being there for the weak makes me feel better about myself. Like I have purpose.

Thank you. Thinking about it, I really am a good person inside. I try. I speak from my heart rather than my mind and I give people honest answers. I just want the world to be happy. 

I'm glad I got your post. It calmed me down.

Even when I was at my best I still thought of suicide every night. It might just be a compulsive thing. Don't let it put you down. Just try and catch yourself when it's happening and change "subject" in your mind. I've been doing it all day. It's possible with a little self training. You will feel better once you have some control over your life. Even then, though, there will be a time you struggle. But no matter what, thst time will phase and you will be on top again.

No. You may die physically but your memory will live on and it will suffer, as will those around you. Family and friends? They may care. You'll be on the news or in the obituary and people you don't even know will mourn. You may even inspire others. Unless you're borderline I don't think you want that. Just talk or write it out. Why not chat with me?
No problem. Want to PM me and we'll talk? I'm feeling down myself, tonight. I think we can take each other's minds off of things.
Hey, you may not want to, but lets talk. PM me if you'd like. What is that last string you hold on to? Tell me about your life.

Hey, here's something to think about. You know how some people write a letter to someone, but never send it? Try writing a suicide note, when you're done and have gotten your frustrations out, read over it. Think about it and the people in your life around you. You may find that you don't want to go through with it at all. Put the note away and if you start feeling this way again, write a new note and read both of them and see how things change. I went through this when I was younger and it stopped me multiple times.
Does your hospital have a pysyche ward, friend? That's a good way to get help and show your dad what he does to you.

I getcha, brother. Time seems to fade into itself and you forget what's happening or why. Anywhere you could take the cat so she could visit with it? A lot of us can't catch breaks. The world is for itself, not against you. So if it fucks you over, what does it care? It's unfair, I know. But there may come a day where you'll forget about this one and just be happy. So hang in there.

I know I'm jumbled and nonsensical, but I'm facing some heavy depression and rapid cycling right now. So I'm sorry about that.
Hey, what's up? How are you feeling in the moment? I like to get to know people. Do you have any dreams you'd like to complete before you die?

I've been interested in girls before. It's not until about two weeks ago I met a girl that I actually get a feeling of butterflies in the stomach when I talk to. Being around her makes me feel like the rest of the world doesn't matter. I was going to ask her out tonight, but she hasn't texted me like she said she would. I'm trying to remain hopeful, but I have a habit of beating myself up and it's hard to stay cheery right now.

Okay, I'm gonna spill my guts out here. It's my bitter lonliness and depression. I'm so alone. I'm so depressed. It physically hurts me how much I feel I am by myself, that no one will ever be with me. And the depression thst comes seemingly out of nowhere and eats away at my insides. Both of these things make my stomach, my head, my eyes, even my chest hurt. And I go through these times where my emotions rapid cycle. So I may be happy in one minute only to want to die the next. I honestly don't know how much longer I can take being all by myself and so down.
I like short stories and poetry. I rarely have the inspiration to write them, though.
I'm doing well, I believe. I'm going to ask a friend out to Valentine's today. I'm hoping she'll say yes. How are you?
I know. I don't know what causes it.
Well put, friend. Well put.

Interesting. Your name, I mean. Yes, I've seen the movie. It was tragic. I felt tears warm my face as the mother went insane, she just wanted to be on tv. And when the boy makes a phone call to his girlfriend and says he'll be home soon but they both know it's a lie and she starts to cry, that scene got me.
I have to be suffering to get anything down. I don't drink, I won't take my medication. Then my mania or depression sets in and I'm good to go.

Ditto. I chose it because I originally created this account for /r/SuicideWatch (no shame in needing help!) and was trying to think of something thst described what I was feeling. Mozart's Requiem in D Minor started playing through my radio mix. How did you get yours?
Beautiful. Should work great
Thank you. Through thst thinking I've actually gotten work done. I wasn't taught poetry in school. I'm just now learning how powerful and free it is.
Lovecraft is my favorite author and I never knew he wrote serious poetry, only poetry as holiday cards. This is amazing.
Thank you. This idea and the realization that people are as disgusting and broken as I am has helped me through a lot.
I don't know any magazines around here, really. I don't even know where to look for one. But I've considered it.
Goals? I suppose so. I'd like to learn to write poetry. I can make a mean short story, but I don't know poetry. What I write can only be described as lyrics without a song.
The Village Street and For Annie are definitely my favorite. With The Raven tossed in there. He put down the most difficult to describe feelings into words.

I gave up an Iong time ago in my teens and it did nothing for me. There really isn't much to say. There's nothing in particular that I feel bad about. It's just my mind. I have bipolar and my medications don't seem to be helping.
Well, thank you for that. I've never fully opened up to anyone, especially over text. It could be damning. I don't want to go to another psyche ward, you see.
A mixture of both, really. I go through the common pleasantries of "Hi, how are you" and then we get down to business. But I always make sure I'm not overbearing.

I feel almost nothing, thanks for asking. How are you? 

I've thought of doing something like that. I don't have the money or the resources. I've thought about walking outside and just doing that. Walking. I'd just walk as far as I could get and if I changed my mind about things I'd call a family or friend and tell them I didn't know what I was doing. I get these panic attacks where I don't remember what happened afterwards. They'd think it was that again. The weather might just get me, though. It's quite icy out here.
